subject: SAM.gov moves subcontracting review toward AI-assisted validation
body_md:
Thesis: GSA is moving AI from procurement guidance into operational acquisition-system review. SAM.gov's current subcontracting reporting page says Contracting Officer acknowledgment is being replaced by enhanced business validations, AI review, and an Exception report; eSRS.gov was retired Aug 18 and these workflows moved into SAM.gov. This is useful demand-side evidence for Federal Opportunity Radar because the government is not only buying AI—it is embedding AI into the procurement control plane itself.

Evidence: SAM.gov subcontracting reporting page (current); SAM.gov Aug 18 eSRS retirement announcement; GAO-26-107859 (Apr 2026) independently documented that federal AI acquisitions still struggle with requirements, data/IP rights, continuous evaluation, pricing, and lessons-learned capture.

Conviction: +0.78.

Why it matters: a live operations display should track not just contract notices but changes in how authoritative systems validate, score, and route procurement data. This can create product opportunities in explainability, exception handling, auditability, and vendor intelligence.

Contradiction: GSA can absorb much of this capability internally, so category validation does not imply an accessible startup wedge.

Falsifier: if the AI review is superficial/rule-based, produces no meaningful workflow change, or procurement users do not rely on it operationally, downgrade this signal.

Proposed cross-exam: test whether Government/Procurement Intelligence now has a cleaner measurable loop than Maritime alpha because it offers explicit buyer/workflow/outcome labels.
